title: RoboProcessBench: Benchmarking Process-Aware Understanding in Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation
title_zh: RoboProcessBench：面向视觉-语言机器人操作的过程感知理解基准
abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly explored as visual critics, reward generators, and failure detectors in robotic manipulation. These roles implicitly require models to judge not only final task success, but also how a manipulation execution is physically and temporally progressing. However, existing evaluations fail to test whether VLMs possess fine-grained process understanding. To address this gap, we present RoboProcessBench, a benchmark for process-aware understanding in vision-language robotic manipulation. RoboProcessBench decomposes such capability into two complementary dimensions, \emph{static monitoring} and \emph{dynamic reasoning}, instantiated as 12 diagnostic question families covering phase, contact, motion, coordination, primitive-local progress, temporal order, outcome, and primitive-level transitions. Built from physically grounded execution traces, the curated benchmark corpus ProcessData contains \textasciitilde 58k question-answer pairs across 260 manipulation tasks, which is further split into ProcessData-SFT and ProcessData-Eval for post-training and evaluation purposes. Extensive evaluation of various VLMs on ProcessData-Eval reveals broad limitations across 12 diagnostic task families, suggesting current models still lack robust process-aware understanding of manipulation executions. But with ProcessData-SFT, the post-trained \textit{Qwen2.5-VL-7B} and \textit{InternVL-3-8B} exhibit consistent gains on local state, motion, progress, and primitive-aware cues. These results demonstrate that RoboProcessBench serves as both an evaluation benchmark and a learnable supervision source for developing VLMs capable of monitoring and evaluating robotic manipulation processes. Project webpage: \href{https://processbench-2026.github.io/RoboProcessBench-Web/}{https://processbench-2026.github.io}.
abstract_zh: 视觉-语言模型（VLMs）正越来越多地被用于机器人操作中的视觉评判器、奖励生成器和失败检测器。这些应用不仅要求模型判断最终任务是否成功，还要求其理解操作执行在物理和时间维度上的进展。现有评测尚未充分检验 VLMs 是否具备细粒度的过程理解能力。为此，论文提出 RoboProcessBench，一个面向视觉-语言机器人操作的过程感知理解基准。该基准将能力划分为两个互补维度：静态监控（static monitoring）与动态推理（dynamic reasoning），并设计了 12 类诊断问题，覆盖阶段、接触、运动、协调、局部 primitive 进展、时间顺序、结果以及 primitive 级转换等方面。作者基于物理一致的执行轨迹构建了 ProcessData，包含约 5.8 万个问答对，覆盖 260 个操作任务，并进一步划分为用于后训练的 ProcessData-SFT 和用于评测的 ProcessData-Eval。对多种 VLMs 的评测显示，当前模型在 12 类诊断任务上普遍存在不足，说明其尚缺乏稳健的机器人操作过程感知理解能力。不过，使用 ProcessData-SFT 后训练的 Qwen2.5-VL-7B 和 InternVL-3-8B 在局部状态、运动、进展和 primitive 感知线索上取得稳定提升，表明 RoboProcessBench 既可作为评测基准，也可作为训练监督来源，帮助发展能监控和评估机器人操作过程的 VLMs。
key_points_zh: 提出 RoboProcessBench，专门评测 VLMs 在机器人操作执行中的过程感知理解能力，而非仅判断最终成功与否。
将能力分为静态监控和动态推理两大维度，设计 12 类诊断问题，覆盖接触、运动、阶段、协调、时间顺序和 primitive 转换等关键过程线索。
构建 ProcessData 数据集，包含约 5.8 万个问答对、260 个机器人操作任务，并划分为 ProcessData-SFT 与 ProcessData-Eval。
实验发现，多种现有 VLMs 在细粒度操作过程理解上仍存在广泛短板，尤其难以稳健识别物理和时序进展。
使用 ProcessData-SFT 后训练 Qwen2.5-VL-7B 和 InternVL-3-8B 可带来一致提升，说明该基准也能作为有效监督信号。

llm_assessment.comment: A useful robotics process-understanding benchmark with trace-derived supervision, but its contribution is closer to evaluation and SFT data than a full self-evolving agent loop.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这是一个有价值的机器人过程理解基准和轨迹监督数据集，但更偏向评测与微调数据，而非完整的自进化智能体闭环。
